| Scene description | • S11-B is in Hubu Alley Food Street. Public facilities and planting alternate along grey stone paving, steps and planters.<br>• In S11-B-02, two stained, rusty yellow square covers lie beside planting and are labelled as waste accumulation; they resemble discarded utility covers or equipment bases.<br>• In S11-B-03, dark brown classification bins labelled ‘Residual waste’ and ‘Recyclables’ stand beside the path. Leaves and miscellaneous items at the openings are labelled as overflow; a cigarette-extinguishing notice is attached.<br>• In S11-B-05, objects covered in wrinkled, partly damaged blue, red and white sheets at a planted edge are labelled as overflowing waste, possibly temporary discarded materials or construction waste. No other obvious classification bins or accumulations are identified; only these three images contain perceived targets. |
| Regulatory basis | • Municipal governments should strengthen sanitation management and maintain clean, attractive and hygienic cities; urban management departments and subdistrict offices are responsible. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 3.<br>• Indiscriminate dumping, stockpiling or scattering of municipal waste on roads, squares, green spaces and other public areas is prohibited; duties include timely collection, classification and proper disposal. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 12.<br>• Busy commercial pedestrian streets should provide classification bins every 300 m and keep them clean and free of overflow or leakage. Standard for the Provision of Urban Environmental Sanitation Facilities, Section 5.2.3.<br>• Collection points should be emptied daily, overflow cleared within 2 hours, and checks, reporting and response linked in a closed management process. Technical Specification for Municipal Solid Waste Collection, Transport, and Treatment, Section 4.1.2.<br>• Improper stockpiling may attract CNY 50–2,000 fines where advice is ineffective, correction is refused or environmental untidiness results. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 36. |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Three overflow locations and one accumulation are localised, without extensive pollution, neglected sanitation areas or obstruction of pedestrian routes. |
| Impact assessment | Visible effects: S11-B-03 overflow may attract insects and cause odours; damaged covers in S11-B-05 may allow waste leakage and impair appearance; uncleared waste in S11-B-02 presents a safety risk. Near-term risks: delayed clearance could cause complaints and harm Hubu Alley’s tourist image; low winter temperatures may allow bacterial growth and increase disease risks. |
| Potential causes | • Capacity or collection frequency may be insufficient: S11-B-03 and S11-B-05 are labelled as overflow in a busy food street. Verify collection records and bin standards.<br>• Temporary-storage management may be lacking: damaged, wrinkled covers in S11-B-05 may conceal construction or renovation waste without barriers or signs. Check recent works or business renovation records.<br>• Facility maintenance may be inadequate: rusty, unlabelled yellow covers in S11-B-02 may be abandoned equipment. Check whether they are municipal or privately installed and establish ownership and responsibility. |
| Long-term effects | Persistent or recurrent problems could expand overflow and accumulation, create neglected areas and encourage insects and rodents; reduce visitor and resident satisfaction and commercial vitality; and increase complaints, penalties or adverse urban-management assessment results. |
| Recommendations | • Immediate action: clear S11-B-02 accumulation and S11-B-03/S11-B-05 overflow, reinforce or replace damaged covers, prevent exposure, and clean the S11-B-03 bin and assess its capacity.<br>• Longer-term action: (1) add bins or collect at least twice daily, especially around meal peaks; (2) register and approve temporary storage, including business renovation waste; (3) identify and dispose of abandoned facilities such as S11-B-02 covers and record ownership; (4) add smart bins or overflow alerts in priority areas. |
| Priority | **High.** Overflow and accumulation in a busy commercial street affect cleanliness and public safety and create sanitation and complaint risks. Complete clearance and correction within 24 hours. |
